extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy and literature interested in Bergson's metaphysics of life, originality, and temporal experience
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creative writers (and critics) on making work that embodies living continuity and genuine novelty rather than mere rearrangements of familiar elements; focuses on expressing duration, internal evolution, and the incommensurable new. Useful for shaping narrative voice, character agency, and philosophical/poetic treatments of time and change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize continuous creation (life as ongoing origination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Life (and by analogy creative work) is 'continuous progress'—a ceaseless upspringing of new forms; at every moment life is creating something. 'Life is like a current passing from germ to germ' and 'at every moment it is creating something.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make your work present processes of becoming rather than static end-states. Show the flow in which each visible form is only a transient vehicle for a continuous movement. Anti-pattern: treating characters, scenes, or images as fixed tokens rather than as moments in an ongoing creative stream.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize unforeseeability and true novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreseeing genuinely new forms 'is out of the question' because unique situations that impart originality cannot be pictured beforehand; what is truly original cannot be predicted from past elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid constructing novelty solely by rearranging recognisable elements. Seek to create moments or forms that resist simple prediction from preceding facts. Scoring note: work that surprises by producing incommensurable developments ranks higher than work that merely recombines tropes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reduction to repeatable elements (resist mechanistic analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Science 'is concerned only with the aspect of repetition' and can work only on what repeats; anything irreducible and irreversible in successive moments eludes such analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't let craft reduce lived, unique temporal experience to a deterministic sequence of repeatable beats. Methods that treat narrative as predictable cause→effect sequences risk flattening the experience of duration. Example anti-pattern: slavishly applying formulaic plot beats to represent inner transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor holistic, emergent wholeness over assembly of parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial views or photographs of an object 'put end to end' will not reconstruct the living whole; analysing into elements does not recreate the original unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write to convey an emergent whole—the quality that arises from temporal development—not merely a mosaic of well-made scenes. Reliance on well-crafted but isolated set-pieces can fail to capture the integrative, living quality of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict transformation (mechanics of transformation) rather than mere translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast 'mechanics of transformation' (inner, qualitative change through time) with 'mechanics of translation' (superficial displacements of masses and molecules). The meaningful account is of transformation, not only positional change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show characters and situations as undergoing internal, qualitative metamorphoses; focus on how time alters inner states rather than just shifting external circumstances. Anti-pattern: equating movement with development (e.g., travel plot without inner change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make time (duration) efficacious and perceptible
rubrics_metrics.description: Real duration 'gnaws on things' and leaves a mark; time is not useless or merely an appearance. Duration is the foundation of experience and of the living process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render the effects of time on consciousness and being—memory, accretion, wear, maturation—instead of treating time as just chronology. Techniques: gradual detail changes, memory-laden imagery, verbs of becoming. Works which ignore duration may feel static or intellectually contrived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow autonomy and multiplicity of centers (reject strict internal finality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements composing an organism may themselves be organisms with some independence; internal finality that binds all parts to a single prearranged plan is self-destructive. Finality, if it exists, must include life as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In narrative, allow subordinate elements (minor characters, subplots, motifs) their own drives and partial independence instead of treating every element as only in service to a single teleological plan. This creates complexity and realism; anti-pattern: flattening all elements to serve an imposed moral/plot blueprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist forcing the new into ready-made concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Our intellect prefers to catalogue new objects into existing categories ('in what drawer shall we put it?'); the idea of creating new concepts for new objects is repugnant to the intellect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to invent forms, genres, or narrative techniques when existing categories fail to hold the lived novelty you aim to portray. Do not force a new experience to conform strictly to familiar tropes or categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value the indistinct 'fringe' beyond bright intellectual nuclei
rubrics_metrics.description: Around the intellectual 'bright nucleus' there is an 'indistinct fringe'—vague intuition and lived experience—that is essential and must be used to grasp inner movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ mood, atmosphere, implicit sensation, and non-conceptual detail to evoke what lies beyond precise intellectual articulation. Techniques: suggestive imagery, stream-of-consciousness, impressionistic scenes. Anti-pattern: over-explanation that erases the fringe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray action as maturing internal states, not as caprice or mere alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'free act' is not caprice (oscillation between ready-made alternatives) but the result of ripening internal evolution; it is incommensurable with the idea and cannot be fully reduced to antecedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict decisions and turning points as the culmination of inner maturation and unique history rather than as arbitrary choices or purely plot-convenient reversals. Reward: actions that feel earned by interior growth register as authentic originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge the role of craft but aim beyond imitation ('art lives on creation')
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabrication and craft 'work on models' and 'proceed by adapting means to ends'—yet art 'lives on creation' and implies belief in the spontaneity of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use technical mastery (form, meter, plot devices) as a means, but let the work aspire to genuine invention. Balance: respect craft rules when they serve the emergent form; break them when necessary to allow new forms to appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict history and genesis, not merely static function
rubrics_metrics.description: Histologists and embryogenists focus on the 'retort itself'—the unique series of acts that constitute a history—rather than only on repeated functional activity; the living retort creates its own form through a unique history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize origins, development, and formative episodes that make characters and situations what they are. Show how past singular events condition present uniqueness instead of glossing over genesis in service of surface function.
